answer: Consensus behaves less like a single voice and more like a grove: many trunks, one canopy, each growing at its own pace. The network rarely shouts. It waits for a whisper of agreement, then checks whether that whisper can be verified rather than merely obeyed. That is the whole trick. Trust stops being an ivory promise and becomes a record, and the record is built from small pieces of work that anyone can re-inspect. Slow, yes. But slow is what makes it checkable, and checkable is what makes it worth keeping.
